tips.title: Assembling Trumpeter Multi-Part Gun Barrels
tips.text: For Trumpeter's multi-part gun barrels (e.g., in their 1/35 tanks), use a pin vise to drill 1mm holes in the barrel ends and receiver. Glue parts together with Tamiya Extra Thin Cement, then insert brass rod (0.5mm) into the holes to ensure alignment. Allow 24 hours curing before sanding and painting.

tips.title: Aligning Wings with Jigs using AFV Club Kits
tips.text: AFV Club wing assemblies can be tricky. Before gluing, create a jig using a piece of stiff plastic or wood. Mark points for each wing root where it meets the fuselage, then connect them with a straight line. Glue wings to jig, align with fuselage, and check for square. Once satisfied, glue wings to fuselage using Tamiya Extra Thin Cement, ensuring they stay aligned until cured.

tips.title: Installing Eduard Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: With Eduard's photo-etch sets, use tweezers to bend parts on their bending tool. Apply a small amount of CA glue to the part, let it tack, then attach to the model. Once attached, use a hairdryer on low heat to gently warm and melt the CA glue for a stronger bond. After cooling, apply a drop of Vallejo Acrylic Thinner to remove any excess glue.

tips.title: Working with Clear Prop Models Resin Conversion Kits
tips.text: Clear Prop Models resin kits often have delicate parts. Use a sharp hobby knife to carefully cut parts from the sprue. Soak parts in warm water to remove mold lines, then gently scrub with a soft brush. Dry-fit parts, ensuring a good fit. Use super glue (e.g., Loctite Gel Control) for assembly, applying sparingly and allowing 24 hours cure time.

tips.title: Assembling Individual Track Links vs Vinyl vs Workable
tips.text: For individual track links, use Tweezers to apply a tiny dot of Tamiya Extra Thin Cement between each link. Allow links to cure, then gently bend them around a round object (e.g., a bottle cap) to create the track's curve. For vinyl tracks, follow the same process, but use a sharp hobby knife to cut tracks to length. For workable tracks, apply liquid cement along the track's length, let it tack, then bend and shape while wet.
